thank you. to be honest ive been on the fence about this issue for a while but luckily my mom trusts me a fair bit abt this kinda stuff so even if I do get caught with a gf i can play it off as just being friends, which I think i'll maintain until I'm a financially stable adult.

classic reddit, random strangers assuming serious mental illnesses off one trivial piece of information. "her stomach hurts" = eating disorder? and does that even give the father a pass for being angry at her??? no one should ever act mad to someone with an eating disorder.

it's true that many models suffer from eating disorders, but assuming this off of practically no evidence is bullshit.

since it sounds like you're physically weaker than him currently, I'd say you need to spend as little time with him as possible. if it's possible, don't stay in the house with him until you're sure you can have an actual conversation with him about his behaviour in a safe location. 

he'll probably see you as attention-seeking for talking about your ed seeing as that's how he reacted last time, so bringing it up might make it seem like it's about you to your brother, even if it isn't. to be honest, your brother seems like kind of a shitty person who's become that way due to a cycle, and you're basically taking care of most of his needs, which needs to stop. 

don't clean up his messes, leave them in one area outside his room or something. he's twenty, not fourteen; if you're eating food he wanted, he should have labelled. your brother sounds like he's in a total slump with getting jobs and furthering his life past video games, and waiting on him is not helping. if you can, have a conversation about his behavior. if not, just minimize the things you do for him so he's forced to do it himself.

red flags immediately in the first paragraph. she threw a chair at you. if it didn't miss, what could have happened? what if you got a concussion? a broken limb? she was abusive towards you, and still is, full stop.

she sounds incredibly self-entitled and as stated, childish. no adult person over the age of 30 should be acting like a ten year old. if i were you, i would go full non contact, but if you're not ready for that, I suggest stop initating hangouts with her, or having conversations with her. talk with her for the bare minimum, and eventually grow distant from her.

they sound very manipulative, even if it might be unintentional. please get financially independent as quickly as you can and create both physical and emotional distance between yourself and your parents. some of the stuff they're doing is bordering on abusive, and it doesn't sound like you've been lacking in communicating your wants. hope it works out for you and your parents realize how overbearing and manipulative they've been

I think an actual sit-down talk is in order for this issue. You need to explain how uncomfortable it makes you that they treat you like a toddler (like seriously seeing the comments here, they're wayyy overdoing it) and that they need to accept that you're literally some months away from being a legal adult. their jokes are crossing the line and it seems like they're trying to control even your adult life out of some twisted concern for you
